content:
Lauren Bishop: Need to lock the beta customer list for tiered Dedicated throughput SLO GA rollout. Goal: 4–6 accounts across tiers/regions + 1 internal dogfood. Please reply w/ candidates + any hard constraints (legal, hardware supply, routing risk). Also: define “success criteria” per account so we’re aligned for the retro.

Lauren Bishop: Draft criteria template (per account):
- Tier + region + shape(s)
- Model(s) + max ctx
- Committed throughput floor (metric)
- Measurement window + exclusions accepted
- What we’ll monitor (dashboards) + who gets access
- “Success” definition (e.g., 99% of 5-min windows >= floor over 14d)
- Escalation expectations + comms cadence

Talia Benson: +1. Also need dates: beta start window + when we consider them “ready” to move from feature flag to default. I’ll turn replies into a tracker + status doc.

Stephanie Nguyen: From GTM side, best candidates are the folks already asking “put it in writing” but still collaborative. I’d avoid anyone mid-procurement redlines until we’ve proven measurement + credits flow.

Rachel Kim: CS POV: we want a mix, but PLEASE include at least one “bursty + noisy neighbor sensitive” account so we validate admission control + comms.

Sean Gallagher: Constraints reminder: for beta we should stick to pinned model versions + single region per deployment (no cross-region failover promises yet). We can still *test* failover, but don’t sell it as entitlement.

Allison Grant: Observability is ready to support 4–6 accounts. If we go beyond that, we’ll need to limit custom panels. For beta, keep it to the standardized dashboard + per-deployment tags only.

Sergio Costa: Dashboard panels we have now:
- `Dedicated Throughput Floor Compliance` (by deployment_id)
- `Saturation signals` (queue depth, GPU util, KV cache hit rate)
- `Exclusions breakdown` (client throttling, 4xx/5xx, warmup)
We can give customers read-only exports weekly; console widget isn’t GA.

Irene Choi: Hardware supply note: us-east A100 and L40S are easy right now. eu-central H100 is tight; can do 1 Premium shape there but lead time risk ~2–3 weeks. us-west H100 OK-ish but we’re using more for Hosted.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1 to Irene. If we want a Premium beta in EU, pick an account that’s ok with a later start date or can run on A100 shape for beta then swap to H100 at GA.

Lauren Bishop: Candidate list I’m thinking (based on pipeline + prior calls):
1) Acme AI (Standard or Plus) – us-east
2) Vidorama (Plus) – us-west
3) BluePeak (Plus) – eu-west/eu-central
4) HyperDoc (Premium?) – us-east
5) Northstar Support (Standard) – us-east
6) (Optional) AlphaBank (Premium) – only if legal ok
Thoughts?

Isabelle Laurent: Acme + Vidorama are great. HyperDoc is in procurement mode; they’ll ask a million questions, but that’s not bad if we’re ready. AlphaBank will absolutely block on contract language + auditability; I wouldn’t put them in beta unless we want the beta to become a negotiation.

Laura Bennett: Finance request: beta should include at least one account where burst will happen so we can validate burst metering + invoice line items BEFORE broader rollout. Also want 1 account with stable load to validate “clean” compliance numbers.

Rishi Malhotra: Agree. For the beta definition of success, include “metering matches SLO metric within X%” so we don’t discover mismatched accounting later.

Rafael Mendes: From SRE: prefer accounts with engaged eng contacts + willingness to share client-side metrics. Biggest time sink in early SLO programs is proving it’s not client throttling / request shape issues. Also: no multi-model deployments for beta unless we’re explicitly testing the attribution rules.

Markus Klein: Solutions notes by account:
- Acme AI: pretty hands-on, will do a benchmark run + can pin to one model version.
- Vidorama: high volume, cost sensitive, runs lots of short prompts + streaming; GREAT for catching token accounting bugs.
- BluePeak: still in POC scoping; might not hit steady state quickly.
- HyperDoc: legal-heavy, but their eng lead is solid. They’ll demand written SLO wording even in beta.
- Northstar Support: smaller but very cooperative; good “Standard tier, no drama” baseline.

Elliot Price: If we include HyperDoc in beta, I want to ensure we’re using the same customer-facing wording as in the docs PR (no bespoke language in Slack/email). Otherwise we’ll create a forked set of promises.

Lauren Bishop: Ok, let’s decide:
- Keep AlphaBank out of beta (too risky)
- Keep BluePeak as “beta waitlist / POC parallel” unless they can commit to a steady test window
- Beta cohort = Acme AI, Vidorama, HyperDoc, Northstar Support + 1 internal dogfood deployment
Need 1 EU account though—do we have someone else besides BluePeak?

Stephanie Nguyen: We can add a smaller EU customer that’s not in procurement hell. I’ll check w/ AEs for who’s in EU and already on Dedicated.

Vanessa Ortiz: If we *must* have EU, we can do eu-west A100 shape beta (more available) and only test Standard/Plus there. Save EU Premium for GA.

Sean Gallagher: That works. SLO semantics don’t change by region, but we’ll learn about telemetry gaps + network effects.

Talia Benson: I’ll put “EU slot = Plus on eu-west A100” as default, pending Sales confirming a willing account. For now, define success criteria for the four named + internal.

Lauren Bishop: Great. Let’s write success criteria per account here so we don’t argue later.

Lauren Bishop: **Acme AI (Plus, us-east)** proposed success criteria:
- Deployment: single region (us-east), pinned model version (TBD by Quentin)
- Shape: A100 80GB x8 (if available) OR L40S x8 fallback
- Workload: mixed chat, moderate ctx (<= 8k), streaming ON
- SLO metric: tokens/sec (completion tokens) aggregated per deployment_id
- Compliance: >= committed floor in 99% of 5-min windows over any rolling 14-day period (excluding documented warmup + customer throttling)
- Instrumentation: customer provides client-side qps + latency; we provide dashboard link + weekly export
- Operational: 0 Sev-1 customer incidents attributable to Redwood capacity; any SLO burn-rate page acknowledged <15 min during biz hours

Sean Gallagher: Minor tweak: define what counts as “documented warmup” (e.g., first 30 min after scale-up / model load) and cap it (like <= 2% of windows). Otherwise it’s too hand-wavy.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also for Acme: success includes “no false positives” from burn-rate alerts. If we page 20x for nothing, it’s not a success.

Allison Grant: We can add: “<2 false-positive pages/week per deployment” as a beta target.

Lauren Bishop: Noted. Adding warmup cap + alert noise target.

Lauren Bishop: **Vidorama (Plus, us-west)** proposed success criteria:
- Region: us-west
- Shape: L40S x8 (preferred) or A100 x8
- Workload: very high QPS, short prompts, heavy streaming, bursty traffic
- Success:
  1) Admission control protects throughput floor under burst (no >10 min sustained periods below floor when within committed RPS envelope)
  2) Streaming token accounting matches customer observed throughput within 5% (post PR-19422 fix)
  3) Burst metering events emitted + match billing export (burst vs committed) for at least 2 weekly cycles

Rishi Malhotra: Love including the billing export check. Add: “Finance can reconcile burst units to raw meter events without manual SQL” (aka the tooling works).

Sergio Costa: For Vidorama, also watch saturation: GPU util pinned at 95–100% for long periods will make us look bad even if we technically meet floor. Maybe add a threshold like “p95 queue time < X ms”?

Sean Gallagher: Careful: queue time isn’t in the SLO. But for beta, we can add a “guardrail success metric” like p95 time-to-first-token stable within agreed range.

Lauren Bishop: Good call. I’ll add a non-contractual guardrail: TTFT p95 not regressing >20% vs baseline week.

Lauren Bishop: **HyperDoc (Premium, us-east)** proposed success criteria:
- Region: us-east
- Shape: H100 x8 if available; A100 x8 acceptable for beta if we adjust floor accordingly
- Workload: longer ctx (<= 16k), lower QPS but strict consistency
- Success:
  1) Written beta addendum (non-binding) aligns to the standard SLO wording + exclusions (no custom carveouts)
  2) SLO compliance >= 99.5% of 5-min windows over rolling 30 days (Premium target) *for the beta window, measured weekly*
  3) Incident comms drill: simulate 1 SLO burn event and validate CS + SRE escalation + customer update within stated timelines

Rachel Kim: Strongly +1 on the comms drill. HyperDoc is exactly the kind of account that will judge us on process, not just numbers.

Elliot Price: Re: “written beta addendum” — please route through Sofia (Legal). Even if it’s “non-binding,” it tends to get forwarded.

Lauren Bishop: Yep, will loop Sofia. For now, we’ll use the standard SLO language from PM-503 draft.

Lauren Bishop: **Northstar Support (Standard, us-east)** proposed success criteria:
- Region: us-east
- Shape: A100 x4 (or smaller standard shape)
- Workload: steady low/medium QPS, mostly non-streaming, short ctx
- Success:
  1) Clean measurement: exclusions <1% of windows (no client throttling ambiguity)
  2) SLO compliance >= 99% of 5-min windows over 14 days
  3) Customer-facing reporting: weekly summary email is understandable + matches console numbers (once widget enabled for internal view)

Allison Grant: For Northstar, this is a good candidate for validating the “simple story” we want to tell: committed floor + what to do when you’re below it.

Talia Benson: **Internal dogfood** criteria:
- Tier: Premium-like settings
- Goal: catch alerting + dashboard issues before customers
- Success: no metric gaps, burn-rate alerts fire in staging drills, and the runbook links from dashboards are correct.

Irene Choi: One more constraint: if HyperDoc ends up on A100 for beta, don’t label it “Premium” in any customer comms; call it “Premium entitlements, beta hardware.” Otherwise they’ll screenshot it.

Lauren Bishop: Good point. We’ll phrase it as “Premium tier program, beta capacity on A100; committed floor set accordingly.”

Stephanie Nguyen: Update on EU slot: I can probably get an EU-based SaaS already on Dedicated to join as Plus in eu-west. Will confirm name in a separate thread (don’t want to spam this one w/ pipeline stuff).

Talia Benson: Action items:
- Lauren: finalize cohort list (4 named + internal) + draft success criteria doc
- Sean/Rafael: confirm warmup cap + alert noise targets are measurable
- Sergio/Allison: confirm dashboards + weekly export format
- Vanessa/Irene: confirm shape availability + lead times (especially HyperDoc)
I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff w/ cohort owners once Sales confirms EU option.

Lauren Bishop: Thanks all. I’ll post the compiled list + criteria in Confluence and link here for final :thumbsup: sign-off.
